memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Your slave is in your hands," Abram said. "Do with her whatever you think best." Then Sarai mistreated Hagar; so she fled from her. - Gen 16:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a painful verse to read. Abram washes his hands of the situation - "do whatever you think best" - abandoning both Hagar and any responsibility. And Sarai, with full power over her slave, mistreats her so badly that Hagar, pregnant and alone, flees into the wilderness. The powerless one becomes the victim of everyone else's failure.

Scripture does not excuse this. It tells the truth about how God's people treated a vulnerable foreign woman. Hagar was a slave, an Egyptian, pregnant, with no rights and no protector. When the family's scheme fell apart, she is the one who suffered most. The strong wronged the weak, and the weak had nowhere to turn.

We must sit with this honestly, because it happens still. When things go wrong, it is so often the most vulnerable who bear the cost - the poor, the powerless, the outsider, the one with no voice. And sometimes, shamefully, it is God's own people doing the wronging.

But here is the wonder of what follows: Hagar flees, and God pursues her. The One the family forgot did not forget her. God has a special heart for the mistreated and the outcast - "a father to the fatherless, a defender of widows" (Ps 68:5). If you have been wronged by the powerful, or overlooked and cast aside, take heart. The God who found Hagar sees you too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you ever been the vulnerable one wronged by others' failures?
- Are you using whatever power you have to protect the weak, or to harm them?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You see the vulnerable ones wronged by the powerful. If I have been mistreated, comfort me; if I hold power over others, help me use it to protect, not harm. Give me Your heart for the weak.
Amen.
